timeline.message: Lexicographic ordering for FileAccessTree with special cases for separators
timeline.author: ldematte

timeline.body:
This PR re-introduce "string" ordering for FileAccessTree, with special cases for directory separators, as the existing based on path iteration was not working on Windows - `WindowsPath` discards the root.

It does still handles paths in a slightly different way between Windows and non-Windows (Posix).
This is because Java supports both \ and / as separators on Windows, but \ is a valid character for file names in Posix - it's very strange, possibly not frequent, but it's a possibility. This means that windows paths will be possibly ordered "wrongly" on a Linux machine; this should not matter, as we won't be matching any path to them.

Fixes #123682, fixes #123655, fixes #123611 and possibly other windows IT tests failures

I'm very torn about this point. See the description for why I did it this way, then come back here :) 

Should we take care of this in normalization? And turn every separator into the "canonical" one for the current platform?
Should we just consider both separators on all platforms and do not care that \ is a file character on posix? (See unit tests) (what does the JDK do here?)

reply.body: I think we should, and do, normalize all slashes into the canonical separator for the platform.

:D I did that, but Intellij suggested to change it this way.
I agree with you though, it's better, and more clear.

timeline.body:
Using `charAt` tends to cause problems for characters outside the basic multilingual plane (like emojis), but I suspect it doesn't matter in this case because we're only comparing for order, not trying to identify the actual characters.

As silly as it sounds, it might be good to have at least one test with an emoji to demonstrate that this logic works with characters outside the BMP.

reply.body:
I added a test and there were no surprises.
I think we are OK here: as you said, as long as the order is consistent we don't care much. One important caveat is that we do not match the "special" char (/ or \) with a random surrogate by mistake, but surrogates are in a whole different range, so that won't be an issue.

timeline.body:
Simply subtracting two integers is discouraged. Instead, `Integer.compare` is recommended.

I think it doesn't matter in this case, because the range of these two values is so limited, but it might be best to call `Integer.compare` so the code doesn't "look wrong".

I realize this javadoc isn't new to this PR, so this is your call...

It might be worth explaining why this wrongness is acceptable. I think it's because this is only for validation, and that if we allow something that looks like an absolute path but isn't, the consequences are minor?
